declaration: void __thiscall EditorAnimWorld_SetTargetAngle_0059cea0(cEditorAnimWorld *this, int creatureID, float angle, bool applyNow);

mechanics: Spill argument 1 and check the map gate this+0x38; a zero gate returns without any map call.

lower_bound against this+0x0c through a valid local cursor out pointer, then find, then TEST ECX,ECX on the mapped controller: a null controller is an additional early return that the lookup miss path produces.
On success load applyNow from [ESP+0x18] and angle from [ESP+0x14], then FSTP the angle onto the outgoing stack so the forwarded call is (controller, angle, applyNow) in that order.
Forward to 0x0059b2f0, which stores the angle at controller+0x44 and, when applyNow is set, also stores it at controller+0x48 and rebuilds the creature orientation row at creature+0x10..0x1c.

evidence.observation: Listing proves the 0x38 gate, the two LEA/PUSH pairs that give 0x00e5c780 a real key pointer and out pointer, the TEST ECX,ECX null-controller exit, the [ESP+0x18]/[ESP+0x14] argument loads, the FSTP stack push and the RET 0xc epilogue.
The forwarded target writes controller+0x44 always and controller+0x48 plus the creature orientation row only when applyNow is non-zero, fixing the argument order.

evidence: 0x00e5c780 stores the found node through [ESP+0x8] and dereferences [ESP+0xc] as the search key, so the native stack order after the receiver is (out, key). The port declaration and both call sites use (map, out, key) with a non-null out pointer and the cursor is read back from that slot.
